meta.title: Versor Robotics | Autonomous machines for the fields of tomorrow
meta.description: Versor Robotics builds farm robots: a collaborative mobile robot that follows you and goes where you guide it, and an autonomous sprayer. Rugged, precise and quietly relentless.
meta.ogDescription: Autonomous machines for the fields of tomorrow.

hero.lede: Autonomous machines for the fields of tomorrow. We build farm robots made for hard work in the field: rugged, precise, and quietly relentless.

vision.title:
Robots that

work inside

crop rows.
vision.lede: Field work is heavy and repetitive, and labour is hard to find and costly. Big machines do not fit between crop rows. A tractor is wider than the row and cannot enter once the crop is up. A drone works from above. A person can reach anything but cannot keep up.

platform.title: One platform
platform.text: A four-wheeled autonomous robot that works inside grown crop rows. Attachments change the job: logistics, spraying, harvesting and crop monitoring.

carrier.text: Our collaborative robot moves around on its own, follows you and carries the load, so your hands stay free. A light touch guides it anywhere, no hard pushing. Tested carrying loads at FPO Anekal and an Army base workshop.

spray.text: Our spraying robot looks at the plant from the side and opens only the nozzles with a leaf in front of them. The whole leaf is wetted and gaps get nothing.

vision.closing: Where we are going: a robot that works with the farmer, not instead of the farmer, built in India for Indian crop rows.

features.title: Power-ups, built in<dot>.</dot>
features.lede: Four capabilities that make a Versor robot feel less like a machine and more like a crew member.

follow.title: Autonomous Follow-Me
follow.text: The robot locks onto its operator and walks the field with them, carrying crates, tools or a full tank. Want it somewhere else? A light touch of the hand guides it there.
follow.diagram: Top-down map: a rover follows its operator around a field

spray.title: Autonomous Spraying
spray.text: Set the rows, press go. The boom drives the lines and sprays along the path with nobody at the controls.
spray.diagram: Top-down map: a spraying rover drives across crop rows and wets them

asr.title: ASR Module
asr.text: Talk to your robot. Onboard speech recognition turns plain spoken commands into actions, even with gloves on and the engine running.
asr.diagram: A spoken command, 'Spray rows three to six', and the robot's spoken reply

waypoint.title: Waypoint Navigation
waypoint.text: Drop pins on the map and the robot drives the route in order: stop by stop, row by row, and back home.
waypoint.diagram: A map with four numbered waypoints; the rover drives them in order

pilots.metaDescription: Two completed pilots of the Versor robot: load carrying on farms with FPO Anekal, and in the workshop at Army Base 515. What we tested and what we learned.
pilots.title: Pilots<dot>.</dot>
pilots.intro: Two pilots have been completed: one on a farm, with FPO Anekal, and one in a workshop at Army Base 515. In both, we tested the robot carrying loads.

drip.title: Drip lines
drip.text: Drip irrigation lines were the biggest obstacle. They run along the beds and cross the paths the robot has to drive on.

spacing.title: Uneven rows
spacing.text: Row spacing is never uniform. It changes from farm to farm, and from one row to the next.

turning.title: Turning
turning.text: Turning width is a bigger problem than row width. Driving along a row is easier than turning at the end of it.
